eras.name: Hundred Years War and the Valois

events.title: The Chauvet cave paintings
events.description: Lions, rhinoceroses and horses are drawn in charcoal on the walls of a cave in the Ardeche, with shading and perspective, twenty thousand years before Lascaux.

events.title: Lascaux
events.description: Some six hundred painted animals cover a cave in the Dordogne. It was found by teenagers chasing a dog in 1940 and closed to the public in 1963 because breath was damaging it.

events.title: The Carnac stones
events.description: Neolithic people in Brittany raise over three thousand standing stones in rows several kilometres long. Nobody knows what they were for.

events.title: Greeks found Massalia
events.description: Colonists from Phocaea in Asia Minor found a trading port that becomes Marseille, and bring wine and the olive to Gaul.

events.title: The La Tene Celts
events.description: Celtic culture with its curling metalwork spreads across Gaul. The Greeks call these peoples Keltoi and the Romans call them Galli.

events.title: The Gauls sack Rome
events.description: A Gallic army under Brennus takes Rome and is paid off in gold. The Romans never forget it.

events.title: Rome takes the south
events.description: The Mediterranean coast becomes the Roman province of Gallia Narbonensis. Its people still call it simply the Province, Provence.

events.title: Caesar invades Gaul
events.description: Julius Caesar begins eight years of campaigning across Gaul, partly to pay his debts, and writes them up in the third person.

events.title: Vercingetorix at Alesia
events.description: The Arverni chief unites the tribes and wins at Gergovia, then is besieged at Alesia behind Roman double walls and surrenders. He is strangled in Rome six years later.

events.title: Lugdunum is founded
events.description: A colony at the meeting of the Rhone and Saone becomes Lyon, the capital of the Three Gauls and birthplace of two emperors.

events.title: The Pont du Gard
events.description: A three-tier aqueduct bridge carries water fifty kilometres to Nimes, dropping about a third of a millimetre for every metre it travels.

events.title: The martyrs of Lyon
events.description: Christians including the slave Blandina are killed in the amphitheatre. It is the first clear record of a church in Gaul.

events.title: The Gallic Empire
events.description: A Roman general proclaims a breakaway empire covering Gaul, Britain and Spain that lasts fourteen years.

events.title: The Rhine frontier breaks
events.description: Vandals, Alans and Suebi cross the frozen Rhine on the last day of the year and sweep across Gaul to Spain.

events.title: Attila is turned back
events.description: Romans and Visigoths stop the Huns at the Catalaunian Plains near Chalons. Legend credits Genevieve with saving Paris by prayer.

events.title: Clovis defeats the last Roman ruler
events.description: The young king of the Salian Franks beats Syagrius at Soissons. A Frankish kingdom replaces Roman rule in northern Gaul.

events.title: The baptism of Clovis
events.description: Clovis is baptised a Catholic at Reims rather than an Arian like the other Germanic kings, which wins him the Gallo-Roman bishops. French kings are anointed at Reims ever after.

events.title: Victory at Vouille
events.description: Clovis drives the Visigoths out of Aquitaine. Paris becomes his capital.

events.title: The battle of Tours
events.description: Charles Martel defeats an Umayyad army between Tours and Poitiers. Later writers made it the moment Europe was saved; at the time it was a large raid repelled.

events.title: Pepin deposes the Merovingians
events.description: The mayor of the palace has the last long-haired king tonsured and sent to a monastery, and is anointed king with papal approval.

events.title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
events.description: Pope Leo III crowns the king of the Franks in Rome. He rules most of western Europe from Aachen, and France and Germany both claim him.

events.title: The Oaths of Strasbourg
events.description: Two of Charlemagne's grandsons swear alliance in each other's language. One text is the oldest surviving document in an early form of French.

events.title: The treaty of Verdun
events.description: Charlemagne's empire is split three ways. Charles the Bald's western share is the ancestor of France.

events.title: Vikings besiege Paris
events.description: A Viking fleet blockades the city for a year. Its defender, Count Odo, is later elected king.

events.title: Cluny Abbey is founded
events.description: A Benedictine house answering only to the pope becomes the head of over a thousand monasteries across Europe.

events.title: Normandy is founded
events.description: Charles the Simple grants the lower Seine to the Viking leader Rollo in return for defending it. His descendants conquer England.

events.title: Hugh Capet is elected king
events.description: The Count of Paris becomes king, ruling little beyond the Ile-de-France. His direct male line holds the throne for 341 years.

events.title: William of Normandy conquers England
events.description: A French-speaking duke becomes king of England, and the French crown now has a vassal more powerful than itself.

events.title: Urban II preaches the crusade
events.description: At Clermont the pope calls for an armed pilgrimage to Jerusalem, and the crowd answers "God wills it". French knights make up most of the First Crusade.

events.title: Gothic at Saint-Denis
events.description: Abbot Suger rebuilds the royal abbey choir with pointed arches and walls of glass. The style spreads across Europe as the French work.

events.title: Eleanor of Aquitaine marries Henry
events.description: Divorced from Louis VII, the heiress of a third of France marries the future Henry II of England. The Angevin empire stretches from Scotland to the Pyrenees.

events.title: Notre-Dame de Paris begun
events.description: Building starts on the cathedral that takes nearly two centuries. It burns in 2019 and reopens in 2024.

events.title: The University of Paris
events.description: The masters and students of Paris are recognised as a corporation. It becomes the leading school of theology in Christendom.

events.title: The Albigensian Crusade
events.description: A crusade is preached against the Cathars of the south. At the sack of Beziers the legate is reported to say: kill them all, God will know his own.

events.title: The battle of Bouvines
events.description: Philip Augustus defeats an alliance of England, the Empire and Flanders. Normandy and Anjou are now his, and the French crown is the strongest in Europe.

events.title: Louis IX and the Sainte-Chapelle
events.description: The king consecrates a chapel of stained glass to house the Crown of Thorns, then leaves on crusade. He is made a saint in 1297.

events.title: The first Estates General
events.description: Philip IV summons nobles, clergy and townsmen to back him against the pope. Five years later he has the Templars arrested on a Friday the thirteenth.

events.title: The papacy at Avignon
events.description: Clement V settles at Avignon and seven popes in a row are French. Petrarch calls it the Babylonian captivity.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: The Hundred Years War begins
events.description: Edward III of England claims the French throne through his mother. The war lasts, with truces, for 116 years.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: The battle of Crecy
events.description: English longbowmen destroy the French cavalry. Calais falls the next year and stays English for two centuries.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: The Black Death
events.description: Plague arrives through Marseille and kills perhaps a third to a half of the population in under three years.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: The Jacquerie
events.description: Peasants north of Paris rise against the nobility after the capture of their king. It is crushed in weeks.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: Agincourt
events.description: Henry V's exhausted army beats a French force several times its size in the mud. Henry is recognised as heir to France five years later.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: Joan of Arc relieves Orleans
events.description: A peasant girl from Lorraine who hears voices lifts the siege of Orleans and has Charles VII crowned at Reims.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: Joan is burned at Rouen
events.description: Captured by the Burgundians and sold to the English, she is tried for heresy and burned at nineteen. She is rehabilitated in 1456 and canonised in 1920.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: The war ends at Castillon
events.description: French cannon destroy the last English army in Gascony. England keeps only Calais.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: Burgundy is absorbed
events.description: Charles the Bold dies at Nancy and Louis XI takes the duchy. The great rival within France is gone.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: The Italian Wars
events.description: Charles VIII invades Italy to claim Naples. Sixty years of war follow, and the Renaissance comes home with the armies.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: Leonardo comes to Amboise
events.description: Francis I invites the aged Leonardo da Vinci to the Loire, where he dies three years later. The Mona Lisa stays in France.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: French becomes the language of law
events.description: The ordinance of Villers-Cotterets requires all legal acts to be written in French rather than Latin. It is still in force.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: The Wars of Religion
events.description: A massacre of Protestants at Vassy opens thirty-six years of civil war between Catholics and Huguenots.

events.era_name: Hundred Years War and the Valois
events.title: The St Bartholomew's Day massacre
events.description: Huguenot leaders in Paris for a royal wedding are murdered, and the killing spreads through the city and the provinces. Thousands die.

events.title: Henry of Navarre inherits
events.description: The last Valois is assassinated and the Protestant Henry of Bourbon becomes king. He converts in 1593, reputedly saying Paris is well worth a mass.

events.title: The Edict of Nantes
events.description: Henry IV grants Protestants freedom of worship and fortified towns. The wars of religion end.

events.title: Champlain founds Quebec
events.description: A French post on the St Lawrence is the start of New France, which at its height runs from Acadia to Louisiana.

events.title: The siege of La Rochelle
events.description: Cardinal Richelieu starves the Huguenot stronghold into surrender after fourteen months. Protestants lose their military independence.

events.title: The Academie francaise
events.description: Richelieu founds a body of forty members to regulate the language. Its dictionary is still unfinished in its ninth edition.

events.title: Descartes publishes the Discourse on Method
events.description: Written in French rather than Latin, it begins from doubt and arrives at I think, therefore I am.

events.title: The Fronde
events.description: Nobles and the Paris parlement rise against the crown while Louis XIV is a child. He never forgives Paris.

events.title: Louis XIV rules alone
events.description: On Mazarin's death the king announces he will be his own chief minister. He reigns seventy-two years, the longest of any European monarch.

events.title: The court moves to Versailles
events.description: A hunting lodge becomes a palace for ten thousand people where the nobility is kept close and busy with etiquette.

events.title: The Edict of Nantes is revoked
events.description: Protestantism is banned and some two hundred thousand Huguenots flee to England, the Netherlands, Prussia and the Cape, taking their trades with them.

events.title: The Encyclopedie
events.description: Diderot and d'Alembert begin publishing a work meant to gather all human knowledge. It is banned twice and finished anyway.

events.title: Voltaire's Candide
events.description: A satire on optimism, the church and war, published anonymously in Geneva and banned on sight. Voltaire denies writing it.

events.title: New France is lost
events.description: The Seven Years War ends with Canada ceded to Britain. Voltaire had dismissed it as a few acres of snow.

events.title: The first manned balloon flight
events.description: The Montgolfier brothers' hot-air balloon carries two men over Paris for twenty-five minutes.

events.title: The storming of the Bastille
events.description: A Paris crowd takes the royal fortress for its gunpowder and finds seven prisoners. The date becomes the national holiday.

events.title: The Declaration of the Rights of Man
events.description: The National Assembly abolishes feudal privilege and declares men born free and equal in rights. Olympe de Gouges answers with a declaration for women and is guillotined.

events.title: The flight to Varennes
events.description: The royal family is caught fleeing in disguise near the border. The monarchy never recovers its credibility.

events.title: Valmy and the Republic
events.description: A volunteer army turns back the Prussians, and the next day the monarchy is abolished. Goethe, watching, says a new era has begun.

events.title: Louis XVI is executed
events.description: The king is guillotined in what is now the Place de la Concorde. Marie Antoinette follows in October.

events.title: The Terror
events.description: Robespierre's Committee of Public Safety executes some seventeen thousand by sentence, while the war in the Vendee kills far more.

events.title: Robespierre falls
events.description: The Convention turns on him and he is guillotined the next day. The Terror ends.

events.title: The metric system
events.description: The metre is defined as a ten-millionth of the distance from the pole to the equator. Most of the world now measures in it.

events.title: Napoleon's coup
events.description: General Bonaparte overthrows the Directory and makes himself First Consul.

events.title: The Napoleonic Code and the coronation
events.description: A single civil code replaces hundreds of local laws, and Napoleon crowns himself emperor at Notre-Dame. The code is copied across Europe and Latin America.

events.title: Austerlitz
events.description: Napoleon defeats the Austrian and Russian emperors on the anniversary of his coronation. It is his most celebrated victory.

events.title: The retreat from Moscow
events.description: The Grande Armee of over six hundred thousand reaches a burning Moscow and retreats through the winter. Fewer than a fifth come back.

events.title: Waterloo
events.description: Back from exile on Elba, Napoleon is defeated by Wellington and Blucher in Belgium and dies on St Helena six years later.

events.title: The July Revolution
events.description: Three days of barricades in Paris replace Charles X with Louis-Philippe. The same year France invades Algeria.

events.title: The conquest of Algeria
events.description: An expedition takes Algiers. Algeria becomes part of France and stays so for 132 years.

events.title: Daguerre and photography
events.description: The French state buys Daguerre's process and gives it to the world for free.

events.title: The Second Republic
events.description: Revolution brings universal male suffrage and abolishes slavery in the colonies. Louis-Napoleon is elected president in December.

events.title: The Second Empire
events.description: Louis-Napoleon makes himself Napoleon III. Haussmann tears down medieval Paris and builds the boulevards.

events.title: Les Miserables
events.description: Victor Hugo, in exile on Guernsey, publishes the novel. It sells out in Paris in a day.

events.title: Sedan and the fall of the Empire
events.description: The emperor is captured with his army by the Prussians, and Paris proclaims the Third Republic. Germany takes Alsace and Lorraine.

events.title: The Paris Commune
events.description: Paris rules itself for seventy-two days. The army retakes it in the Bloody Week and kills perhaps ten thousand.

events.title: The first Impressionist exhibition
events.description: Monet, Renoir, Degas and others show the work the Salon rejected. A critic names them after Monet's Impression, Sunrise.

events.title: Free, secular schooling
events.description: The Ferry laws make primary education free, compulsory and secular.

events.title: The Eiffel Tower
events.description: Built for the centenary exhibition and condemned by artists as a monstrosity, it was meant to come down after twenty years.

events.title: The Dreyfus affair
events.description: A Jewish army captain is convicted of treason on forged evidence. Zola's J'accuse splits the country, and Dreyfus is exonerated in 1906.

events.title: The Lumieres' first film show
events.description: The brothers screen ten short films to a paying audience in a Paris cafe basement.

events.title: Church and state separate
events.description: A law ends state recognition of religion. Laicite becomes a founding principle of the Republic.

events.title: The Marne
events.description: The German advance is stopped forty kilometres from Paris, helped by troops rushed to the front in taxis. Four years of trench war follow.

events.title: Verdun
events.description: Ten months of fighting around the fortress city kill some three hundred thousand. They shall not pass.

events.title: The Armistice
events.description: Germany signs in a railway carriage at Compiegne. France has lost 1.4 million men.

events.title: The treaty of Versailles
events.description: Germany is made to accept guilt and pay reparations, and Alsace-Lorraine returns to France.

events.title: The Popular Front
events.description: Leon Blum's left-wing government brings in the forty-hour week and paid holidays. The working class goes to the beach for the first time.

events.title: The fall of France
events.description: Germany breaks through the Ardennes and France falls in six weeks. Petain signs an armistice in the same railway carriage.

events.title: De Gaulle's appeal from London
events.description: An almost unknown general calls on the BBC for the French to keep fighting. Few hear it at the time.

events.title: Vichy
events.description: Parliament gives Petain full powers and the Republic ends. His regime collaborates, and deports some seventy-six thousand Jews.

events.title: D-Day
events.description: Allied troops land in Normandy. Paris is liberated in August.

events.title: Paris is liberated
events.description: The French 2nd Armoured Division enters Paris, and De Gaulle walks down the Champs-Elysees.

events.title: Women vote for the first time
events.description: French women vote in municipal elections, decades after Australia and New Zealand.

events.title: The European Coal and Steel Community
events.description: Robert Schuman's plan pools French and German coal and steel so war between them becomes impossible. It grows into the European Union.

events.title: Dien Bien Phu
events.description: The Viet Minh overrun the French base in northern Vietnam. France leaves Indochina.

events.title: The Algerian War
events.description: The FLN's uprising begins eight years of war, with torture by the French army and terror on both sides.

events.title: The Fifth Republic
events.description: Recalled during the Algerian crisis, De Gaulle gets a constitution with a strong presidency. It is still in force.

events.title: The French bomb
events.description: France tests an atomic bomb in the Algerian Sahara and becomes the fourth nuclear power.

events.title: Algeria is independent
events.description: The Evian accords end the war. Nearly a million pieds-noirs leave for France within months.

events.title: May 68
events.description: Student occupations and a general strike of ten million workers nearly bring down the government. De Gaulle wins the election that follows and resigns a year later.

events.title: Mitterrand and the death penalty
events.description: The first socialist president of the Fifth Republic abolishes capital punishment. The last execution by guillotine had been in 1977.

events.title: Maastricht passes by a whisker
events.description: A referendum approves the European Union treaty with 51% of the vote.

events.title: The Channel Tunnel
events.description: Britain and France are joined by rail beneath the sea for the first time.

events.title: The franc gives way to the euro
events.description: Notes and coins in a currency shared with eleven other countries replace the franc.

events.title: The Paris attacks
events.description: Islamic State gunmen and bombers kill 130 people at the Bataclan, cafes and the Stade de France, ten months after the Charlie Hebdo killings.

events.title: The Paris Agreement
events.description: Nearly every country agrees to hold warming well below two degrees.

events.title: Notre-Dame burns
events.description: Fire destroys the roof and spire. The cathedral reopens in December 2024.
